items.label: text
items.text: There are advantages and disadvantages for using either method to dispose of plastics.

items.label: table
items.text:
| Disposal method   | Advantages                                                                                | Disadvantages                                                                                                                                               |
|-------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Landfill          | No greenhouse gases or toxic gases produced from plastics Cheap                           | Ugly, smelly and noisy; no one wants to live next to a landfill site Uses large areas of land The waste will be there for thousands of years                |
| Incineration      | Requires little space Can produce heat for local homes/offices and/or produce electricity | It is expensive to build and maintain the plant Produces greenhouse gases Releases toxic gases The ash produced must still be disposed of in landfill sites |

items.label: text
items.text: When a lot of ethene molecules combine to make a chain, the double bonds break and the monomer molecules just add onto each other to make a polymer. Nothing is lost. That is why it is called addition polymerisation.

items.label: text
items.text: Making a polyester is different. Instead of one type of monomer, you often hav        i   a small molecule such as water or hydrogen chloride is lost. The elimination of water gives the name condensation to this type of polymerisation.

items.label: text
items.text: One of the monomers is a diol, an alcohol molecule with one -OH at each end. For example, ethane-1,2-diol has the structural formula CH2OHCH2OH. The prefix 'eth' indicates the presence of two carbon atoms in the molecule. The code 'di' in the name shows that there are two -OH groups present. The number '1,2' tells you the -OH groups are attached to carbons number 1 and 2, one on each carbon. Propane-1,3-diol, which has one more carbon in the carbon chain, has the structural formula CH2OHCH2CH2OH.
